statement: The pair $(\mathcal M,W)$ admits a theory of $W$-homotopy fibres, and $\mathcal H=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$.
gap_or_error: This is a standing hypothesis inherited from Chapter XII, not a claim that an arbitrary relative category has homotopy pullbacks.
repair: For the model-category comparison, use derived pullbacks of fibrant cospans. Keep the earlier class $\mathrm{Fib}_W$ distinct from an unqualified class of Quillen fibrations.
notes: The source uses category of models in its localizer framework; ordinary Quillen hypotheses must be stated when invoked.

statement: An ordinary square in $\mathcal H$ is designated h-cartesian exactly when it is isomorphic in $\operatorname{Fun}(\square,\mathcal H)$ to the image of a $W$-cartesian square in $\mathcal M$.
repair: This image-class definition is meaningful. It asserts existence of a suitable coherent lift; it does not make every strict or coherent lift cartesian.
notes: Repeated on manuscript p.8; audit once here and distinguish it from Proposition 1.

statement: In the assumed fibre theory a designated square has a representative $Y_3=Y_1\times_{Y_0}Y_2$ with both base arrows in $\mathrm{Fib}_W$.
gap_or_error: Fibrant-object hypotheses must not be omitted when translating this sentence into a general Quillen model category.
repair: Replace the cospan by fibrant objects and its legs by fibrations; an ordinary pullback then computes its derived pullback. The postface explicitly supplies the model-category qualifications.
notes: No transcription error is inferred from the abbreviated fibre-theoretic notation.

statement: For a strict pullback square, one base arrow in $\mathrm{Fib}_W$ suffices to obtain a $W$-cartesian square.
gap_or_error: Correct in the assumed homotopy-fibre theory; for arbitrary Quillen fibrations the blanket statement needs fibrant objects or right properness.
repair: Use a fibration $Y_1\to Y_0$ with $Y_0,Y_2$ fibrant; right properness permits dropping those fibrancy requirements. Do not silently strengthen the scope beyond the source hypotheses.
notes: The symmetric assertion follows by interchanging the two legs.

statement: Quadrangulated structures are proposed as a nonadditive analogue of triangulated categories, but ordinary homotopy-category squares retain too little structure for the intended theory.
gap_or_error: This is a structural diagnosis, not a theorem asserting equivalence with triangulated categories.
repair: The postface makes the loss precise: the image in an ordinary functor category does not determine whether a chosen lift is a homotopy pullback.
notes: Do not read too weak as saying every proposed axiom is weak: Cart(3) and Cart(5b) are too strong for the coarse image class.

statement: The finer category $\mathrm{HO}_W(\square)=\mathcal M^{\square}[W_{\square}^{-1}]$, and analogous categories for $\Phi$ and $\Psi$, are the appropriate homes for coherent squares and their homotopy limit properties.
repair: In the derivator repair, cartesian coherent squares are the essential image of right Kan extension from the punctured square. Underlying ordinary squares are obtained by a separate diagram functor.
notes: The positive observation is not refuted by the failure of Proposition 1.

statement: An axiomatisation retaining those diagram categories and their relationships, independently of a chosen model presentation, leads toward derivators.
gap_or_error: The manuscript does not propose a formal uniqueness theorem for all possible enhancements or axiomatizations.
repair: Read as motivation for coherent diagram categories and Kan extension axioms; modern derivators and infinity-categories provide different precise realizations.
notes: Not classified as an unresolved mathematical problem.

statement: A left quadrangulated category is a category $\mathcal H$ with a distinguished class Cart of ordinary commutative square diagrams, subject to Cart(1)–(5).
repair: Use an ambient universe, or a class of squares when the category is large. The definition is consistent: ordinary pullbacks give examples.
notes: The open-ended phrase Cart(…) reflects axioms being developed, not an additional axiom.

statement: Cart(1): transposition of a square preserves membership in Cart.
repair: Satisfied by ordinary pullbacks and by the homotopy-image class; for coherent squares it follows from symmetry of the square shape.
notes: Source status is assumed because this is part of the definition, not a proved theorem about its intended example.

statement: Cart(2): in a commutative square with base leg $p_1$ invertible, the square belongs to Cart if and only if its opposite leg $q_1$ is invertible.
repair: The homotopy-image class satisfies this: pulling back an equivalence preserves equivalence, and a square with both specified opposite edges invertible is isomorphic to a trivial square.
notes: The corresponding assertion for the other pair of edges uses Cart(1).

statement: Cart(3), composition direction: if the left and right squares of a commuting two-square rectangle belong to Cart, their outer rectangle belongs to Cart.
repair: Valid for the homotopy-image class of every Quillen model category. Lift the common ordinary-arrow isomorphism to the homotopy category of arrows, realize the two square maps on a shared bifibrant middle arrow, and apply coherent pasting. Fullness and conservativity of the arrow comparison, used for the model category and its arrow category, preserve the cartesian lifts. A complete rectification proof is in the commentary.
notes: Positive composition is proved in the commentary using standard arrow rectification. Christensen--Frankland Proposition 6.11 also proves it for arbitrary triangulated categories. The postface refutes cancellation only.

statement: Cart(3), cancellation direction: if the left square and the outer rectangle belong to Cart, the right square belongs to Cart.
gap_or_error: Fails for the intended class of ordinary squares admitting a homotopy-cartesian lift, as the postface proves.
repair: Retain a single coherent rectangle: then the homotopy pullback pasting/cancellation theorem applies. Ordinary isomorphism classes of the individual squares discard the required compatible coherence.
notes: The axiom remains assumed as a formal definition; the counterexample is separately audited below.

statement: Cube corollary: if the bottom and all four lateral faces of a commutative cube belong to Cart, its top face belongs to Cart.
gap_or_error: No error; the proof is left implicit.
repair: Paste the bottom with an opposite lateral face, then cancel the other lateral face against the resulting rectangle. Cart(1) allows the required orientation of Cart(3).
notes: A formal consequence of the axioms, regardless of their failure in the proposed homotopy-image example.

statement: For the cube corollary, the bottom face and two opposite lateral faces already suffice.
gap_or_error: No gap beyond the omitted elementary pasting argument.
repair: For a cube $X\to Y$, paste $B=(X_1\leftarrow X_3;Y_1\leftarrow Y_3)$ with $Y$, obtaining $R=(X_1\leftarrow X_3;Y_0\leftarrow Y_2)$. Cancel $F=(X_0\leftarrow X_2;Y_0\leftarrow Y_2)$ from $R$ to obtain $X$.
notes: This is the stronger version asserted in the first footnote.

statement: Any ordinary square isomorphic to a square in Cart also belongs to Cart.
repair: The lateral squares of an isomorphism cube belong to Cart by Cart(2); the cube corollary transfers membership from one horizontal face to the other.
notes: The source names Cart(3) and Cart(2). Symmetry may be tacit in choosing an orientation; this is not a substantive error.

statement: The preceding stability axioms appear to exhaust the useful stability properties, so further such properties should be consequences.
gap_or_error: No formal language or class of properties is specified, so this is not a well-posed completeness theorem.
repair: Treat as a methodological expectation. The commentary proves particular consequences rather than assigning a present-day open status to an unspecified completeness claim.
notes: The text explicitly presents an impression, not a proved result.

statement: Cart(4): every cospan in the category admits a completion belonging to Cart.
repair: For the homotopy-image class, represent the two homotopy-category arrows on suitable replacements and take a homotopy pullback. Unlike a square, the cospan shape has no nontrivial commutativity relation to rectify.
notes: This is an existence axiom, not yet a unique universal property.

statement: Cart(4) together with the announced exactness axiom will make distinguished completions of a fixed cospan unique up to isomorphism.
repair: Cart(5a) provides a map over the identity boundary, and Cart(5b) makes it an isomorphism; Corollary 1 supplies this argument immediately afterward.
notes: This anticipatory statement is later proved. It does not assert uniqueness of the comparison isomorphism.

statement: Cart(5a): every morphism of the three-vertex boundary cospans of two distinguished squares extends to a morphism of the entire squares.
repair: With constant squares distinguished, this is equivalent to every designated square being an ordinary weak pullback. Conversely, the target weak pullback supplies the fourth map from the source apex; the source square need not be designated.
notes: The homotopy-image class satisfies this existence requirement even though Cart(5b) fails.

statement: Cart(5b): in every morphism between distinguished squares, if the three boundary components are isomorphisms, the fourth component is an isomorphism as well.
gap_or_error: The intended homotopy-image class violates this universal assertion: its zero endomorphism of a nonzero loop object gives a counterexample.
repair: For coherent cartesian squares, restriction to the boundary detects equivalences between cartesian objects. Formally, Cart(5b) is already a consequence of Cart(1)–(3), as the commentary proves.
notes: Every extension is required to be invertible, not merely the existence of some invertible extension.

statement: Corollary 1: between two distinguished completions of the same cospan there exists a comparison inducing the identity on the boundary, and every such comparison is an isomorphism.
repair: Apply Cart(5a) and Cart(5b) to the identity boundary map. Cart(4) is needed for existence of completions, but not for this conclusion once both completions are given.
notes: The proof is the explicit specialization made by the manuscript.

statement: A comparison isomorphism between distinguished completions need not be unique; a square automorphism may be the identity on its boundary without being the identity at its apex.
gap_or_error: The manuscript supplies no example satisfying all five literal axioms. Such automorphisms occur in the intended homotopy-image class, which fails those axioms.
repair: The formal corollary proves invertibility, not uniqueness. The commentary proves uniqueness whenever binary products exist. It neither produces a nonordinary model of the full axioms in complete generality nor proves general collapse without extra hypotheses.
notes: Do not declare this globally false from the additive special case; record the limited status explicitly.

statement: For a commutative square $Y$ and object $T$, the two projections define $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y_3)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y_1)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y_0)}\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y_2)$.
repair: This is the comparison map for the ordinary representable functor. Surjectivity for every T means weak pullback; bijectivity for every T is the ordinary pullback universal property.
notes: No derived mapping object is being used in the displayed formula.

statement: Corollary 2: for a distinguished square, the representable comparison map is surjective for every test object T.
repair: The manuscript applies Cart(5a) to a constant source square. The same weak universal property holds for the homotopy-image class: compatible homotopy classes admit a path between their composites, supplying a homotopy-coherent cone.
notes: Cart(5b) is not used in this proof.

statement: The constant square on T, all four arrows identities, belongs to Cart.
repair: Apply Cart(2) since the first base arrow and its opposite arrow are identities.
notes: This implicit use of Cart(2) is the only membership input in the proof of Corollary 2.

statement: A map from the constant boundary cospan at T to the boundary of Y is exactly a compatible pair of maps to its two outer vertices; its extensions correspond exactly to preimages under the representable comparison.
repair: The boundary map to $Y_0$ is forced to be the common composite, and specifying the apex component $T\to Y_3$ supplies precisely the two required projection equalities.
notes: This identifies the quantifiers and completes the source proof of surjectivity.

statement: The surjective representable comparison is generally not bijective; designated h-cartesian squares are generally not ordinary pullbacks.
gap_or_error: True for the intended homotopy-image class, but that class does not satisfy all five literal axioms. No full-axiom nonordinary example is supplied here.
repair: A loop square exhibits noninjectivity in genuine homotopy theory. Under the literal axioms, the commentary proves collapse whenever the category has binary products, including the additive case. The completely unrestricted case is not settled in this audit.
notes: The source assertion is not silently promoted to a verified existence theorem for a nonordinary model of all the axioms.

statement: A right quadrangulated structure, or class of h-cocartesian squares, is the dual notion obtained by applying the left axioms in the opposite category.
repair: Reverse all arrows and interchange pullbacks with pushouts, weak terminal cone conditions with weak initial cocone conditions.
notes: The dual definition is mathematically unproblematic.

statement: Left and right structures often occur on the same category, and one should identify additional properties relating them.
gap_or_error: The observation that they often coexist is motivational; their compatibility is not implied by either axiom system.
repair: For coherent derivators, pointedness provides suspension and loop, while stability characterizes coincidence of coherent cartesian and cocartesian squares. Ordinary pullback and pushout structures give a separate bilateral example.
notes: Treat as a programme with precise later replacements, not a single formally open conjecture.

statement: If the underlying category is additive, the h-cartesian and h-cocartesian classes should coincide.
gap_or_error: Additivity alone does not imply stability, even with both literal quadrangulated structures.
repair: In $\mathrm{Ab}$ with ordinary pullbacks and pushouts, the square with base $A\ne0$ and its other three vertices zero is cartesian but not cocartesian. Coherent equality requires stability; Groth2013 also gives an additive nonstable derivator in Example 5.3(2).
notes: The source explicitly marks this expectation as tentative.

statement: In the pointed setting there is a suspension-loop adjunction $\Sigma\dashv\Omega$, associated to the right and left structures respectively.
gap_or_error: The source does not construct the functors or prove the adjunction here. Bare ordinary-square axioms cannot model their intended nontrivial homotopical meaning.
repair: Pointed model categories and pointed derivators have the genuine derived adjunction. For the literal axioms, rigidity forces the completion of zero-to-X-from-zero to have apex zero, and dually suspension is zero; the corresponding formal adjunction is vacuous.
notes: Do not call the standard pointed homotopy-theoretic adjunction false; distinguish its framework from the aborted axioms.

statement: An internal or external Hom should turn h-cocartesian variation in its first, contravariant argument into an appropriate cartesian property.
gap_or_error: No precise enrichment, closure or derived adjunction is specified in this paragraph.
repair: For derived mapping spaces, mapping out of a homotopy colimit gives the corresponding homotopy limit. A closed derived internal Hom has the analogous property under its stated monoidal/adjunction hypotheses.
notes: This is a programme, not a theorem based merely on the availability of an underlined Hom symbol.

statement: An internal or external Hom should preserve the relevant h-cartesian property in its second, covariant argument.
gap_or_error: The paragraph does not specify sufficient adjunction or enrichment hypotheses.
repair: Derived representable mapping-space functors preserve homotopy limits; a derived internal Hom does so when it is a right adjoint in the appropriate closed setting.
notes: The first- and second-variable questions are distinct and are audited separately.

statement: A category having all ordinary pullbacks becomes left quadrangulated by declaring precisely its pullback squares distinguished; all five axioms hold.
repair: The universal property gives symmetry, the isomorphism test, pasting and cancellation, existence, and a unique map of pullbacks for every boundary morphism. Inverse boundary maps give inverse apex maps.
notes: The source calls these familiar properties essentially tautological; it does not write the individual proofs.

statement: In some sense the general case ought to reduce to the elementary ordinary-pullback case.
gap_or_error: No mathematical meaning of reduction is specified.
repair: The commentary supplies a precise local consequence: if a boundary cospan already has an ordinary pullback, every designated completion is that pullback; with binary products all designated squares are ordinary.
notes: The proved commentary statements are distinct from a proof of every possible interpretation of the informal expectation.

statement: The proposed second family of left quadrangulated examples is the localized category with the homotopy-image class of squares, for localizers admitting homotopy fibres.
gap_or_error: As a proposed example of the full axiom system it fails: the editors disprove Cart(3) cancellation and Cart(5b). The image class itself remains well-defined.
repair: Use coherent squares for the full law. The homotopy-image class itself retains symmetry, the trivial-square test, cospan completion, weak universality, and positive composition, but not cancellation or the universal fourth-vertex assertion.
notes: The manuscript explicitly acknowledges that the axiom verification has not been supplied.

statement: Proposition 1 is expected to hold under further hypotheses to be identified, including every presentation quillenizable on finite poset diagram shapes.
gap_or_error: The promised extra hypotheses are never stated; the claimed inclusion of the Quillen-model situation is refuted by pointed model categories with nonzero loop objects.
repair: No added condition covering all those model categories can rescue the assertion. The correct replacement changes the target from the ordinary square category to a category of coherent diagrams.
notes: The reference to XIII, p.51 concerns the intended model-presentation hypothesis, not a proof of the asserted reflection property.

statement: Proposition 1, sufficient direction: if a strict square $X$ in $\mathcal M$ is $W$-cartesian, its image $\mathrm{ho}_W(X)$ belongs to the designated h-cartesian class.
repair: This is immediate from the definition of the image class: the square itself provides the required representative.
notes: The source explicitly calls this direction clear; it is not affected by the counterexample.

statement: Proposition 1, necessary direction: if $\mathrm{ho}_W(X)$ belongs to the designated h-cartesian class, the chosen strict square $X$ is $W$-cartesian.
gap_or_error: An ordinary square may have both homotopy-cartesian and noncartesian coherent lifts. Isomorphism after forgetting coherence does not reflect the chosen lift’s cartesianness.
repair: The postface gives the loop-square and strict zero-square counterexample. In the coherent diagram category, cartesianness is invariant under isomorphism; the ordinary diagram functor is the point at which the conclusion fails.
notes: The printed proposition is preserved as a source error and is not corrected away as a transcription error.

statement: A strict square $X$ in a Quillen model category is homotopy cartesian iff it admits a pointwise weak equivalence $X\to Y$ to a strict pullback with $Y_1\to Y_0$ a fibration and $Y_0,Y_2$ fibrant.
repair: This is the fibrant-cospan computation of a derived pullback. Replace the cospan and use the induced comparison from the original apex; its being a weak equivalence is exactly the homotopy-cartesian condition.
notes: The postface recalls the criterion without reproducing its model-category proof. A directed comparison can be chosen, not merely an unspecified zigzag.

statement: In a right proper model category, the fibrancy requirement on the two specified objects can be omitted from the strict-pullback criterion.
repair: Right properness makes pullback along a fibration preserve weak equivalences, so arbitrary strict pullbacks along fibrations compute homotopy pullbacks after replacement.
notes: The fibration hypothesis is retained; right properness is not claimed for every model category.

statement: Equivalently, for every pointwise weak-equivalence replacement of the boundary cospan by a fibrant cospan with one leg a fibration, the induced map from the original apex to its ordinary pullback is a weak equivalence.
repair: Derived pullback is independent of the chosen fibrant replacement. Hence the existential criterion and the universal replacement criterion detect the same coherent square.
notes: Every refers to compatible replacements of the boundary cospan, not every arbitrary strict square having the same image in the homotopy category.

statement: A pointed model category has an object 0 which is both initial and terminal.
repair: Use 0 or the manuscript’s star consistently. Its initial and terminal properties provide the unique zero arrows used in the counterexample.
notes: The zero object is fibrant and cofibrant, since its identity is both a fibration and a cofibration.

statement: For fibrant $X$, factor $0\to X$ as $0\xrightarrow{\sim}C\twoheadrightarrow X$.
repair: The model-category factorization axiom provides a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration, hence the indicated weaker requirement. Because X is fibrant, C is fibrant as well.
notes: No right properness assumption is needed for this construction.

statement: The loop object is represented by $\Omega X=C\times_X0$.
repair: This is a model of the homotopy pullback of the pointed cospan zero-to-X-from-zero. Different permitted factorizations give equivalent coherent loop squares.
notes: The apex retains the loop information; its two ordinary projections alone do not record the relevant coherence.

statement: The strict pullback square with vertices $C,\Omega X,X,0$ is $W$-cartesian.
repair: Its left leg C-to-X is a fibration and X and 0 are fibrant, so it satisfies the recalled strict-pullback criterion.
notes: This is the positive coherent lift used throughout the counterexample.

statement: In $\operatorname{Fun}(\square,\mathcal M[W^{-1}])$, the loop square is isomorphic to the square with vertices $0,\Omega X,X,0$ and all edges zero.
repair: The weak equivalence zero-to-C makes C isomorphic to zero in the pointed homotopy category. All morphisms from or to this zero object are zero, so this vertex replacement yields an isomorphism of ordinary squares.
notes: This ordinary square is designated by the image definition even when its strict zero-edge lift is not homotopy cartesian.

statement: The strict zero-edge square with apex the loop object is not generally homotopy cartesian.
gap_or_error: It fails whenever $\Omega X\not\simeq0$.
repair: The postface computes its canonical comparison with the genuine loop pullback: it is the zero endomorphism. A concrete pointed-space or chain-complex choice makes this noninvertible.
notes: This proves failure of Proposition 1, not failure of the definition of the coarse image class.

statement: Fixing the three boundary components of the displayed cube uniquely determines its apex component s3 into the genuine strict loop pullback.
repair: The target is an ordinary pullback in the model category, so the two prescribed apex projections determine exactly one strict map s3.
notes: This is strict uniqueness before localization; it does not assert unique maps between arbitrary coarse h-cartesian squares.

statement: If the strict zero-edge square were homotopy cartesian, its canonical comparison s3 with the genuine loop pullback would be a weak equivalence.
repair: Apply the universal replacement criterion to the boundary replacement zero-to-C, together with the identity maps on X and zero.
notes: The boundary replacement has exactly the fibrancy and fibration properties required by that criterion.

statement: The canonical comparison $s_3:\Omega X\to\Omega X$ factors through the ordinary pullback $0\times_X0\cong0$, hence is the zero endomorphism.
repair: The prescribed map into C factors through zero, and the other prescribed map already targets zero. Their strict pullback therefore forces s3 to be the zero map.
notes: The ordinary pullback zero-times-X-zero is zero in every pointed category; it is not the homotopy pullback.

statement: If the zero endomorphism of $\Omega X$ is a weak equivalence, then $\Omega X\to0$ is a weak equivalence.
repair: Write r:P-to-0 and s:0-to-P. In the arrow category r is a retract of sr=0_P, via (1_P,s) and (1_P,r); closure of weak equivalences under retracts proves the implication. Conversely two-out-of-three proves that r weak implies 0_P weak. The commentary gives this argument without cofibrancy or saturation assumptions.
notes: The converse also holds by two-out-of-three, though the postface uses the stated direction.

statement: For a pointed CW complex X in the usual weak-homotopy model structure on pointed spaces, its loop space is weakly contractible iff the connected component of the base point in X is contractible.
repair: Weak contractibility of the loop space kills the fundamental group and all higher homotopy groups of that component. Whitehead’s theorem for CW complexes turns the resulting weak equivalence to a point into a homotopy equivalence.
notes: Other connected components of X are unrestricted; replacing this by contractibility of all of X would be an error.

statement: For unbounded complexes in a Grothendieck abelian category, with quasi-isomorphisms as weak equivalences and the usual derived model structure, the loop object is weakly zero iff X is acyclic.
repair: In the derived category $\Omega X\simeq X[-1]$ in cohomological convention. Its being zero is therefore equivalent to vanishing of all cohomology groups of X.
notes: Use all complexes and the stable derived model structure. The same formulation for connective complexes alone would require modification.

statement: The notation $*_{\Omega X}$ denotes the unique endomorphism of $\Omega X$ factoring through the zero object.
repair: It is the zero morphism, not the identity or an arbitrary based self-map. This label is the essential map in both editorial counterexamples.
notes: The diagrams must preserve this label and its arrow direction exactly.

statement: In the two-square editorial rectangle, the left square and the outer rectangle are both designated h-cartesian ordinary squares.
repair: Both ordinary squares are the zero-edge square identified with the image of the genuine loop pullback. Inserting the zero endomorphism across the additional top edge does not change their zero outer edges.
notes: This statement concerns membership in the coarse image class, not cartesianness of the strict zero-edge lift.

statement: The right square of that rectangle is not in the coarse h-cartesian class when the loop object is not weakly zero, because membership would force its top zero endomorphism to be invertible.
repair: Its bottom edge is the identity of zero. For any genuine homotopy pullback square with one base leg an equivalence, the opposite edge is an equivalence; ordinary square isomorphism preserves that conclusion.
notes: This uses the valid homotopy pullback isomorphism test, not the disputed cancellation axiom.

statement: A model-category morphism which becomes invertible in the homotopy category is a weak equivalence.
repair: This is saturation of the weak equivalences of a model category; apply it to the represented zero endomorphism.
notes: Saturation need not hold for an arbitrary unsaturated relative category, so retain the Quillen-model hypothesis.

statement: The displayed rectangle disproves the cancellation implication of Cart(3) for the coarse homotopy-image class.
repair: Choose a pointed model-category object with nonzero loop object. The left and outer squares satisfy the designated-image definition, whereas the right square fails its isomorphism test.
notes: The axiom is not contradicted within its formal models; this proposed example is excluded by the counterexample.

statement: The cube whose horizontal faces are the same designated loop-image square, whose boundary components are identities, and whose apex component is zero disproves Cart(5b) for the coarse class.
repair: All boundary maps are isomorphisms and the cube commutes because its square edges are zero. The apex zero endomorphism is not invertible for a nonzero loop object. Coherent maps between cartesian lifts cannot have these specified incompatible data.
notes: Cart(5a), the existence of at least one extension, is not disproved: the identity apex extension is available in this same example.

statement: Under Cart(1)–(3), every map between designated squares which is invertible on the three boundary vertices is invertible at the apex; thus Cart(5b) is redundant.
repair: Paste the source square with the lateral square formed by two known boundary isomorphisms; cancel the target square; apply Cart(2) to the remaining lateral face.
notes: Commentators’ formal deduction, not a separately stated source theorem. No existence axiom is used.

statement: A designated square whose boundary cospan already admits an ordinary pullback is itself an ordinary pullback.
repair: Let q:Q-to-P be the comparison with the ordinary pullback and let s:P-to-Q be a weak-universal lift. Then qs is the identity, while sq is an invertible idempotent by Cart(5b), hence the identity.
notes: Commentary adaptation of the standard right-minimal weak-limit argument; Krause explicitly states the minimal-weak-kernel case on p.6 of the March 2014 version. No novelty claim.

statement: Under Cart(1)–(5), a designated square with a monomorphism among its two base arrows is an ordinary pullback.
repair: Paste it with a designated weak kernel pair of the opposite projection. The outer cospan has an ordinary pullback because the original leg is monic, so rigidity makes one kernel-pair projection invertible. A weak diagonal makes both projections equal, proving monicity and hence uniqueness.
notes: Commentators’ development, marked \ours in the block. Complete proof supplied; not found in the limited sources/search checked, with no priority claim.

statement: If the category has binary products and satisfies Cart(1)–(5), it has all ordinary pullbacks and Cart consists exactly of those pullback squares; in particular this holds in every additive case.
repair: Complete $C\xrightarrow{\Delta}C\times C\xleftarrow{f\times g}A\times B$. The diagonal is monic, so the preceding result makes this an ordinary pullback, and its apex is the pullback of f and g. Rigidity plus Cart(4) and isomorphism invariance identify the classes.
notes: Commentators’ development, marked \ours. Binary products suffice; neither a terminal object nor additive enrichment is assumed in the theorem.

statement: In any pointed category with the literal left structure, loop completions are zero; dually suspension is zero. If both structures exist and their designated classes coincide, every object is zero up to isomorphism.
repair: The cospan zero-to-X-from-zero has ordinary pullback zero, so rigidity determines its designated completion. Coincidence also designates that square cocartesian, and dual rigidity for its all-zero span forces its remaining vertex X to be zero.
notes: Commentators’ development, marked \ours. This is an obstruction to the literal ordinary-square axioms, not a theorem asserting that stable homotopy theories are trivial.
